summary: The root قَلَعَ (qalaʿa) primarily means to pull, pluck, tear, or wrench something out or up, detaching it from its place. It signifies removal, displacement, or uprooting.
lane: 1 قَلَعَ ذ and He pulled, plucked, tore, wrenched, or rooted, out, or up, or off; detached; removed from his or its place; displaced; (Msb, K *;) eradicated; uprooted; unrooted. (K.) -b2- تَقْلَعُ (K in art. جذو ) and تقلعُ السَّيْرَ (TA in that art.) [app. for تَقْلَعُ فِى السَّيْرِ ], said of she-camels, (K ib.) [app. They raise their feet clear from the ground: see قَلِعٌ and قُلْعٌ : the pret. seems to be قَلِعَ : so if تَقْلَعُ be the right reading: but in a copy of the K it seems to be تُقْلِعُ : see جَاذٍ , art. جذو .
